geometry.feet: every y in a path or a hall is the FEET level: the first air block above the floor
geometry.tube: as data/rift_mines.json geometry.tube: each segment sampled at n = ceil(4 * horizontal length) + 1 points, each stamping the (2r+1)^2 columns round (floor(x+0.5), floor(z+0.5)) from feet floor(y+0.5) up `height` blocks
geometry.hall: for each column within R(1+ragged)+1 of the centre: d = hypot(dx, dz), theta = atan2(dz, dx), n = 0.5 sin(3 theta + p0) + 0.3 sin(5 theta + p1) + 0.2 sin(7 theta + p2) with p_k = h32(seed, len(id), sum of the id's code points, k) / 2^32 * 2 pi (h32 as tools/rift_mines.py), Rt = radius (1 + ragged n) + 0.5; the column is in when d <= Rt; q = d / Rt; feet = hall feet + floor(bowl q^2 + 0.5); top = max(feet + 3, hall feet + floor(height sqrt(1 - q^2) + 0.5)); carved from feet to top inclusive
geometry.face: the box is never carved; it is written whole: the host (meteorid) everywhere, then for variant k the cells sorted by h32(seed, sum of the face id's code points, k, x, y, z): the first `radiated` cells within 1 of the front become radiated meteorid, the first remaining front cell on the bottom row (not on the box's side columns) is the visible crystal facing out, and the next crystals-1 cells at least 2 deep and under the top row are the hidden ones. The build writes variant 0 once (the restore, and its other variants, are retired: SOUTHERN_RIFT_MEGA.md 13)
geometry.road: each segment of [x, z, y] points sampled as a tube; every column within `half` (Chebyshev) of a sample's rounded point takes the rounded y of the nearest sample (Euclidean, to the unrounded point); ties keep the first. The cove's paths are rasterised the same way
geometry.band: each listed point [j, x, z, nx, nz] claims the columns within 1 (Chebyshev) of (floor(x + nx d + 0.5), floor(z + nz d + 0.5)) for d = -wall.spread_out .. wall.spread_in; a column keeps the claim with the least talus drop, max(0, -d - wall.core), the first among equals (points in list order, d ascending). Its top: in the plug's columns (|j| <= plug.half_j) plug.top_y; elsewhere the crest (wall.top[0] at the first point to wall.top[1] at the last, linear in j, rounded half up) less h32(seed, x, z, 63) mod wall.jag, less wall.batter * max(0, -d - wall.core); rock from the column's top + 1 up to max(that, top + wall.min_rise), unless the column already stands at or over it
geometry.earthworks: square, yard, road and cove path columns (in that order of precedence) get their surface block at the stated y, fill under it down to the ground, and air from y+1 to max(ground, y) + clear_above
geometry.cove: a cove building writes its rect's columns; a house's floor is the highest top under its rect, its door the middle of its door side (x0..x1 or z0..z1 halved, rounded down), and its steps the 3 columns across the door's line at 1, 2 and 3 out, standing at the floor, floor - 1 and floor - 2; a headframe's legs stand at the rect's corners, its shaft collar round the centre; a heap or a pile is a cone over the rect's inscribed circle; a sluice runs along its rect's long side; a lamp post writes its column
geometry.shell: every cell within 2 (a 5x5x5 cube) of the carved space or a face box, not carved, not a face box, and at or under its column's top (an earthwork's surface where there is one, else the ground) is written as rock
geometry.zone: a column is in the zone when its centre (x + 0.5, z + 0.5) is inside the polygon (even-odd rule); each z row's runs are merged down the rows while identical, and every box runs y -64 to 575

farm_tiers.field_why: The Mega field (the owner, 2026-10-03; docs/world-building/MEGA_FIELD.md section 4). The owner's rule is relative: 'if cap after gym 5 is 50 ... lvl 60 or so, so it takes a team' (SOUTHERN_RIFT_MEGA.md:657), so the cap plus about 10 for the outer tier and plus 17 for the deeper (60 and 67 over a cap of 50). The field lies inside Z2 (8 badges, data/rift_zones.json), where the cap is 60 (docs/mechanics/LEAGUE_LEVEL_CAP.md section 2: after gym 8 and through the Elite Four), so the same rule gives 70 and 77. If the owner instead cuts a gym-6 zone out of Z2 for the field (SOUTHERN_RIFT_MEGA.md:706-709, still held), the same rule gives the old outer and deeper levels, 60 and 67: one line each here. A Mega is a Mega form (about 100 more base stats than its line) 10 to 17 levels over the party's cap, so one partner at the cap does not beat it alone (ASSUMED until EXP-054 A6 times a win). Drop rates and respawn are section 13's, unchanged (ASSUMED, untimed).

farms_why: The Mega field (the owner, 2026-10-03): 'everywhere in the red inside the rift should be the mega area ... an aggressive and hostile resource farm ... fight high level megas that in theory should require more than one mon to kill and get a reward to spend in the big town next to this area in the rift.' Packed to its floor 2026-10-04 (the owner: 'Megas are clashing over territory -- not seven dens in a field but a region where they are everywhere, pressing against each other for space ... overlapping ranges'): 61 dens in 16 farms (2026-10-05: the west floor added, below), the 23 land Megas the Cutters sell a stone for that the client draws dealt over them in bands (mega_field.layout.roster), laid out by `python tools/mega_field.py sites` on the canonical heightmap, never a world: anchors packed as close as two lairs allow (lair_spacing 43), each Mega's range (leash) 36, so every range overlaps a neighbour's by 8 or more (layout.min_overlap) and the borders between them are dressed as contested ground (data/mega_borders.json, step R9MB). Inside the field and 36 off its edge, 54 off Victory Road's walked line (layout.why.road_clear, 2026-10-05: was 149), 60 off the gulch zone, in a Rift zone (z2), on a pad level to within one block. Species and tier are both banded by distance from the Cutters' square: the nearest 24 are field_outer (level 70), the 37 at 400 or more field_deeper (level 77). `python tools/mega_field.py floor` measures the floor and the ranges. Every den is dressed as a lair (data/mega_dens.json, step R9MD). The material chain is section 13's unchanged: a defeated Mega rolls its tier's drop of one raw mega_showdown:mega_stone, owner-only, spent at the Cutters in the Cutters' Gulch next door (2 raw and a diamond a keyed stone). NO ZONE on any farm, as decision B4 (2026-10-01): the level band is the gate inside the field, and the field lies inside Z2 (8 badges, data/rift_zones.json). A farm is field_<col>_<row> of 192-block squares; its approach box is its dens' extent plus 64, and the ground of their whole ranges, clipped to farms_grid. A den's id is gm_mf_<x>_<z>, its anchor's column, never its species (2026-10-04: a species may hold several dens); every keeper tag, score, lair function and border is named by it, and no new den reuses a retired den's id.
superseded_farms_why: The open-air Mega farms (the owner, 2026-10-01): 'Mega Pokemon walking in the OPEN, not only in caverns -- a player should see them before they reach them.' Seven dens across the Rift's two southern arms, four outer and three deeper, keeping the material chain and the Cutters exactly as designed: a den's Mega rolls the same raw-stone drop at its tier's rate, and the keyed stone is still cut at the Cutters inside the badge-gated gulch. What changes is that the fight is on open ground a player can see across, not in a hall they have to be let into. NO ZONE on any of the seven -- decision B4 (the owner, 2026-10-01): 'drop the zone on the open dens. A turn-back in open country reads as an invisible wall. Let the level band gate them; being seen and too strong is the point.' So no farm declares a `zone`: there is no polygon, no turn-back point, no zone advancement and no badge-flag check of its own anywhere in the farms. THE GATE IS THE LEVEL BAND ALONE -- outer level 60, deeper 67 (farm_tiers) against a level cap of 50 after gym 5 -- and the only thing that stops an underlevelled party is losing the fight. Nothing is hidden and nobody is bounced: a player at any badge count can walk up to a den, see what it is and try it. The badge flag still gates the GULCH itself (this file's own `zone`, the rockslide gate at gulch_mouth), which is a different thing and untouched: the Cutters who turn a raw stone into a keyed one are inside it, so a stone won in the open is worth nothing until that gate opens. The halls' two Megas (megas.slots) stay as they are: the owner said not ONLY in caverns. Sites measured off the canonical heightmap, never a world (CLAUDE.md): inside the arm polygons of data/regions.json, pad slope under 10 degrees, 24+ clear of every keep_clear box, 260+ apart so finding one is an event rather than a checklist. The sightline measurement that chose them saturated at its own 136-block ceiling for all twelve candidates, so it proves each has a long clear approach and did NOT rank them: spacing and arm coverage picked these seven. The east arm holds the gulch, its road and the Cutters, so it carries the outer tier; the west arm had nothing in it at all, so it carries the deeper tier and the longest walk.

farms_grid.why: The box every farm coordinate (each den's anchor, each approach box corner) must sit in, checked by tools/gulch_mine_audit.py. Re-derived 2026-10-03 from the Mega field, not from the dens: x and z are mega_field.polygon's extent, y the field's ground range (round heightmap) + 1 less approach_below and plus approach_above (`python tools/mega_field.py sites` prints it). The farms write no blocks, so the block-write `grid` is untouched and still never looks at a den.

superseded_farms_grid.why: The box the farms' ANCHORS and approach boxes live in -- not a block box. (It bounded the turn-back points too until decision B4 dropped the zones; the box itself is unchanged, and the audit still bounds a turn-back point for any farm that declares a zone.) The farms write no blocks at all: a den is a keeper line and a leash line, and nothing in them places a single block. `grid` stays exactly as tight as it was, because it guards block writes and must keep doing so; widening it to admit these coordinates would have weakened the one guard that keeps this build inside its box, and a threshold widened to make data pass is not a threshold (CLAUDE.md). So the audit checks block writes against `grid` and farm coordinates against this.

trace.why: The field is the Rift basin (derived/rift_sculpt/plan.json ring, the lip) south-west of the gulch: from the gulch zone's south-west end the ring runs away from the gulch round the inner arm, the islands' edges and the south-west basin, and up the west wall to the ring point nearest cut_near; a straight cut across the stem then joins the gulch zone's north-east end, and the gulch zone's own closing line closes the field, so the two zones share that edge and never overlap. cut_near is the west-wall ring point nearest the gulch line's north-east end (measured 2026-10-03: ring 6902, 319.7 blocks), the stem's narrowest crossing from there; the owner's map did not show where the field stops up the stem, so this cut is the first thing he confirms. `python tools/mega_field.py trace` re-derives polygon and columns Where the simplification would cut a lip column its run vertex is kept, and where even the unsimplified outset misses one (the sculpt's smoothed normal there runs nearly along the lip) that vertex and three either side are set square to the ring instead (mega_field.py trace, lip_kept and lip_squared; 2026-10-03, after the independent audit found 14 basin columns outside): nowhere else does the polygon differ from the plain simplified outset, and the dens and farms are unchanged.

why.road_clear: 54 = leash 36 + aggro_reach 16 + road_margin 2 (the owner, 2026-10-05, review 64: 'make sure to use the left side of the southern tip as well, not just secluded in those pockets': Megas along Victory Road). A den's range (its leash disc round the anchor) ends 18 from Victory Road's walked line; a Mega at its range's edge notices a player aggro_reach away, so a player within road_margin of the walked line (half the road's width 4 where it comes down, data/rift_sculpt.json entrances victory_road_descent.width) is outside every resting Mega's notice: the road runs BETWEEN territories, never through one. aggro_reach is ASSUMED: vanilla 1.21.1 Mob.createMobAttributes() FOLLOW_RANGE 16.0, the reach a NearestAttackableTargetGoal searches; that Cobblemon's PokemonEntity keeps it and Fight or Flight targets by it is NOT VERIFIED (no FoF jar or source in the checkout; EXP-054). The leash is walked back every megas.leash_every_ticks 40, so a Mega chasing someone can overrun its range for up to 2 s. Replaces 149 = 128 + lair_radius (the lairs' critical-path rule): a lair's write box now comes within 54 - 21 x sqrt 2 = 24 of the walked line, never onto it, and the keep_clear discs (the gatehouse post, the descent) are unchanged. tools/mega_dens_audit.py and tools/mega_field_audit.py still hold 128 (their author re-points them); tools/mega_borders.py still writes nothing within 128 of a critical path, so a border nearer the road is undressed
why.gulch_clear: 53 = 32 + lair_radius 21 (a lair keeps 32 from the gulch's zone, mega_dens_audit footprint rule); `sites` takes the larger of it and leash 36 + megas.spawn_clear 24 = 60, so a leashed Mega never comes within 24 of the gulch zone and never wanders into the Cutters' town
why.keep_clear: the same 59 round the two things inside the field that are not ours to crowd: z2's gate post (a lair keeps 32 from a Rift zone post, + its 27) and the descent the road comes down
why.edge_clear: 30 = 21 x sqrt 2, rounded up: a lair's whole write box lies inside the field; `sites` takes the larger of it and the leash, so a Mega's whole range is the field's floor and its approach box never climbs the rim
why.pad: every column within pad_radius 3 of the anchor within pad_relief 1 of the others on the heightmap (round(h), tools/ground.py): data/mega_dens.json anchor_pad's measured precedent, so the keeper spawns on level ground
why.farm_cell: the dens are grouped into farms by 192-block squares of the field so each farm's approach box (the dens' extent + approach_margin 64, the old dens' 64; y -24..+32 round the anchors as before, clipped to farms_grid, the field's own extent) drives only its own keepers
why.roster: SOUTHERN_RIFT_MEGA.md 6.1's rule: a Mega whose line can be had here (its stone is on a Cutters bench, data cutters.benches) and not one of the client's broken Mega models (docs/research/CLIENT_MODEL_FIXES.md: Aggron, Altaria, Gengar, Manectric, Sceptile, Slowbro, Swampert; Pidgeot and Skarmory share a defect) nor a Legends Z-A Mega whose model is unverified; and a land Mega (Gyarados and Sharpedo left out: the field is dry). That is these 23. DEALT in bands (2026-10-04, the owner: 'a region where they are everywhere'): with more dens than species, den k of n by distance takes species floor(k x 23 / n), so a species holds one or more neighbouring territories and the order never goes back. A den is keyed by its own id (gm_mf_<x>_<z>), never by its species: the keeper, its lair's function, its borders and its retirement all name the den. BANDED by distance from the town, nearest first: the scavengers and ghosts at the edge (Sableye, Banette, Absol, Houndoom), the brawlers, the bugs, fire, electric and ice through the middle, the heavy evolved lines section 13 asks for deepest (Steelix, Metagross, Garchomp). Charizard is Mega X here
why.lair: lair_radius 21 is a lair's write box half-width (data/mega_dens.json bounds_why: anchor +- 21, ground - 8 .. + 14; 2026-10-04, from 27: the lairs' measured reach was 14 to 23 blocks, the 23 their 24-block approach track, which mega_dens.json layout.approach_to now ends at 20). Every column in it must have ground within its span: no lower than the anchor's ground - 6 and no higher than + 7 (lair_below, lair_above). lair_spacing 43 = 2 x 21 + 1: no two write boxes touch (tools/mega_dens_audit.py record rule), the closest two dens can stand
why.leash: 36, each Mega's RANGE (the keeper walks it back past it). The owner, 2026-10-04: 'Megas clashing over territory ... overlapping ranges'. With homes 43 to 60 apart a neighbour's range reaches 12 to 29 blocks into this one's, so the borders are shared ground; 36 is short of 43, so no Mega's range reaches its neighbour's home. Raised from 32, where homes 64 apart never overlapped
why.packing: `sites` lays candidates every candidate_step 2 blocks, packs them greedily in seven sweep orders (rows, columns, both reversed, two diagonals, hashed) at lair_spacing, improves each by 1-for-2 swaps, and keeps the order that places most (then most usable floor in a range). It then works the winner for REACH, the owner's 'everywhere' (up to reach_rounds rounds): each den moves to the candidate that adds most usable floor (inside the polygon, dry, no step over one block: the audit's floor) to the ranges if that beats where it stands, keeping a neighbour within 2 x leash - min_overlap; every candidate that still fits is added; 1-for-2 swaps that lose no floor are taken. A den whose range overlaps no other by min_overlap is given a neighbour if one fits, else dropped. The limit is the floor under the lairs' rules (road_clear, edge_clear, the pad, the lair's ground span), no longer the roster: `mega_field.py floor` and `sites` print both
why.deeper_from_town: tier by distance from the Cutters' square (town.square.centre), the reward sink: a den this far or farther is the deeper tier. The owner, 2026-10-04: 'outer/deeper by distance from the town'. ASSUMED, a design threshold set so the inner arm's near half is outer and its far end and the south-west lobe are deeper
why.min_overlap: 8: every den's range overlaps another's by at least this many blocks (homes at most 2 x 36 - 8 = 64 apart), the owner's 'pressing against each other for space' (2026-10-04). Below it a lens is a sliver the border dressing cannot use: its scar's half-width is 3 either side (data/mega_borders.json border.half_width) and nothing is written within 9 of an anchor. It fixes the 2026-10-04 layout's two dens (Steelix, Charizard) whose ranges overlapped nobody (73 apart against 72)

dressing.why: Every field den is dressed as a lair (data/mega_dens.json, step R9MD), because the owner asked on 2026-10-02 to 'see something from the air and go down to it' and section 13 describes the field as 'caves, Mega dens, broken houses half sunk, debris'. A field den takes the KIT of one of the seven 2026-10-02 lairs (their records are data/mega_dens.json superseded_dens): its sign, feature, palettes and signature, so nothing in the builder or its audit is new. Which kit: Houndoom's charred ash and bone heap for Houndoom, Banette, Charizard and Blaziken; Tyranitar's crater for Absol, Medicham and Metagross (a meteor's); Manectric's fused strike for Camerupt and Ampharos; Aggron's spoil heap of torn ore and iron for Scizor, Sableye and Steelix; Pinsir's felled trunks for Heracross, Gallade and Venusaur; Abomasnow and Garchomp keep their own. `python tools/mega_field.py dress` prints the records; only their geometry is per den. 2026-10-04: the six species the field's 23 dens added take Pinsir's felled trunks (Lopunny, Audino, Beedrill), Abomasnow's frost (Glalie), Tyranitar's crater (Gardevoir) and Aggron's spoil heap (Blastoise); tools/mega_dens.py now runs a kit's own behaviour (Tyranitar's split boulders, Abomasnow's snow) for every den dressed with it, where before it keyed them on the den's own species. 2026-10-04 (later): a lair is keyed by its DEN (data/mega_dens.json dens[].den, its function mega_dens/<den>), and a border's two palettes are its two dens' own records, so two dens of one species are two lairs dressed with one kit.

superseded_farms_reason: Superseded 2026-10-03 by the Mega field (mega_field; docs/world-building/MEGA_FIELD.md). The owner, on the map: 'everywhere in the red inside the rift should be the mega area, not just spawn one randomly in the world.' These seven were sited inside data/regions.json's rift_south_west_arm and rift_south_east_arm subregion polygons, which take in the plateau round the basin; all seven stand on high ground outside the basin (y121-148), 163 to 1,133 blocks from the nearest of the owner's coordinates, and none is inside the field. Kept, not deleted: the records hold the 2026-10-01 siting and the B4 reasoning, and staging has had them applied (R9S, R9MD), so their anchors say where a keeper may still have left a Mega and a lair stands. 2026-10-04: the 11 dens of 2026-10-03 (farms field_*, ids gm_field_<col>_<row>_<n>) joined them when the field was packed to its floor with 23 dens whose ranges overlap (the owner, 2026-10-04); their ids are not reused (the new dens are gm_mf_<species>), so R9SX removes any Mega a keeper left at them. Their lairs, if R9MD ever wrote them, are blocks and stay where they stood: no step removes a lair 2026-10-04 (later): the 23 dens of gm_mf_<species> joined them when every den was given its own id, independent of species (gm_mf_<x>_<z>, the anchor's column), so a species can hold several territories, and the field was filled further (27 dens). None of the 23 ids is reused. 2026-10-05: the field re-laid at 61 dens when Victory Road's clearance was re-derived for the owner's west floor (layout.why.road_clear); the 27-den layout's dens that did not survive by id joined these, and no new den reuses a retired id.
